guide.summary: Dubai's Frame, art districts, gardens and safari park, with breakfast cafés, dinners and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Jameel Arts Centre is free but its site lists Tuesday as a closing day, so plan Al Jaddaf and Alserkal Avenue visits for another day.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Jameel Arts Centre's site lists Tuesday as closed, Trèsind Studio lists hours Monday to Saturday only, and Orfali Bros serves dinner Wednesday to Monday.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Dubai Frame sells tickets online (adults AED 50, children 3-12 AED 20, under 3 free), and Dubai Miracle Garden sends tickets as a WhatsApp QR code scanned at the gate. Dubai Safari Park passes start at AED 50.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: 3 Fils at Jumeirah Fishing Harbour says no reservations are needed, while Zuma, Orfali Bros, Mimi Kakushi and Honeycomb Hi-Fi take bookings through SevenRooms.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Dubai Frame bans food, drinks, pets and smoking, and large bags and strollers must be left at the Gate 4 counter; under-12s need an adult. Zuma's lounge is for over-21s in the evening, and Dubai Miracle Garden bans drones and outside food.

guide.dek: Book timed sights like Dubai Frame and the evening restaurants ahead, and keep Tuesdays away from Jameel Arts Centre.
intro: You can get a strong first read of Dubai at Dubai Frame in Zabeel Park, which the site says is supervised by Dubai Municipality. It opens daily from 8:00 am to 9:00 pm, including weekends and public holidays, with hours that may change during Ramadan and holidays. Tickets are sold online at AED 50 for adults and AED 20 for children aged 3 to 12. Leave large bags and strollers at the Gate 4 counter, and note that food, drinks, pets and smoking are not allowed inside.

For art, Jameel Arts Centre on the Jaddaf Waterfront is free and open-access. Its Artist's Rooms for Walid Siti, Lulua Alyahya and Shezad Dawood run from 20 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, and a Salah Elmur exhibition opens on 31 October 2026 and runs to 14 March 2027. The site lists Tuesday as closed. Across town in Al Quoz, Alserkal Avenue is open every day from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m., though individual venues set their own hours, and its food weekend runs 31 October to 1 November.

Families have outdoor options. Dubai Safari Park in Al Warqa 5 opened Season 8 on 12 October 2026 and runs until 31 May 2027, open 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM with last entry at 5:00 PM. Dubai Miracle Garden in Al Barsha South 3 opens 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily, bans drones and outside food, and lists a concert on 21 November 2026. The Green Planet at City Walk opens every day from 10 AM to 6 PM.

For food, 3 Fils at Jumeirah Fishing Harbour takes walk-ins from noon, and Orfali Bros at Wasl 51 Mall serves dinner Wednesday to Monday with set menus from AED 295. Trèsind Studio at St. Regis Gardens on the Palm runs two seatings, at 6:00 PM and 9:15 PM. For an early start, RAW Coffee Company's Al Quoz café opens daily at 7:30am. After dark, you can try Mimi Kakushi, open until 2AM, or CÉ LA VI, 54 floors up at Address Sky View.
summaryCards: Start at Dubai Frame in Zabeel Park, then see the free exhibitions at Jameel Arts Centre on any day but Tuesday.
Take a 7:30am coffee at RAW Coffee Company in Al Quoz, then walk Alserkal Avenue once it opens at 10 a.m.
Reserve Trèsind Studio, Zuma or Orfali Bros ahead, but walk straight into 3 Fils from noon.

limitations: This is a website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several major sites could not be read automatically and were left out rather than bypassed: Burj Khalifa, At.mosphere, The Espresso Lab, Dubai Aquarium, Dubai Opera, SALT and Sky Views returned HTTP 403; the Dubai Culture museum sites (Etihad Museum, Al Shindagha) and Bageri Form and Arabian Tea House returned certificate or SSL errors; Atlantis Aquaventure timed out; Nightjar Coffee and Mirzam were rate-limited; Coca-Cola Arena sent a queue page. Museum of the Future says it is temporarily closed with no reopening date. Global Village, LEGOLAND Dubai, Souk Al Seef and The Dubai Mall published hours or seasons but no street address on the pages read. Some confirmed places are published only partly: Orfali Bros gives dinner days without times, Comptoir 102 shows no 2026-dated content, Jameel Arts Centre's hours conflict with its Tuesday closure, CÉ LA VI and Al Fanar give location descriptions rather than street addresses, and Alserkal Avenue lists entrances rather than a single address. No bakery could be confirmed, so the bakeries list is empty, and only one coffee roaster was confirmed. The total of 17 confirmed places is below the 25-35 target.

2026-10-25: the page was re-read in a browser and its full HTML searched; no AI-directed text was present.
